steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 07:59 in Madrid**.

1. **Date check:** October 24, 2026 is indeed a Saturday. Six days later is Friday, October 30, 2026, which matches the page.
2. **Pacific time on Oct 30:** US daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. On October 30, Pacific time is still PDT (UTC−7).
   - 23:59 PDT on Oct 30 = **06:59 UTC on Oct 31**
3. **Madrid time on Oct 31:** European summer time ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. By October 31, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
   - 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = **07:59 on Oct 31**

The time difference is 8 hours that week, not the usual 9, because Europe changes its clocks a week before the US.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The coming Monday is **November 2, 2026**. By then both cities have left daylight saving time:

- **Madrid:** the EU switched back on Sunday, October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
- **Los Angeles:** the US switches back on Sunday, November 1, 2026, so LA is on PST (UTC−8).

10:00 PST is 18:00 UTC, which is **19:00 in Madrid**. The cities are 9 hours apart, not the usual 8 you'd see for most of the year.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon ends on **Monday, October 26, 2026 at 17:00** Madrid time.

Daylight saving time ends during the event. On Sunday, October 25, 2026, Spain moves its clocks back one hour, at 03:00 summer time (CEST), which becomes 02:00 winter time (CET).

- **Start:** Saturday, Oct 24, 18:00 CEST, which is 16:00 UTC
- **Plus 48 hours:** Monday, Oct 26, 16:00 UTC
- **Converted to Madrid time:** 16:00 UTC is 17:00 CET

So the end time on the clock is 17:00, not 18:00, because of the extra hour gained that Sunday.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time**.

1. **Start time in UTC:** On October 26, 2026, Pacific Time is still on daylight saving time (PDT, UTC−7), which ends November 1 in the US. So 10:00 AM PT = 17:00 UTC on October 26.
2. **Add 72 hours:** 17:00 UTC on October 29, 2026.
3. **Convert to Madrid:** Spain leaves summer time on October 25, 2026 (last Sunday of October). So on October 29 Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). 17:00 UTC = 18:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The results are announced on **November 2, 2026 at 16:59** Madrid time.

1. **Submission deadline:** October 31, 2026 at 23:59 Eastern Time. US daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. So on October 31, Eastern Time is still EDT (UTC−4). That makes the deadline **November 1, 03:59 UTC**.
2. **Add 36 hours:** That gives **November 2, 15:59 UTC**.
3. **Convert to Madrid time:** EU summer time ended on October 25, 2026. Madrid is therefore on CET (UTC+1), which gives **16:59** local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **15:59 on Monday, 12 October 2026**, Tokyo time.

1. **Split into days and time of day:** 1,791,788,340 ÷ 86,400 = 20,738 whole days, with 25,140 seconds left over. 25,140 seconds is 6 h 59 min, so the UTC time is 06:59.
2. **Find the date:** 1970-01-01 to 2026-01-01 is 20,454 days, which leaves 284 days into 2026. Counting from January 1, that lands on 12 October 2026.
3. **Convert to Tokyo time:** UTC is 2026-10-12 06:59. Japan Standard Time is UTC+9 and has no daylight saving, so this becomes 15:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **03:30 on Sunday, 25 October 2026**, Madrid time.

- The "Z" means the time is given in UTC.
- 25 October 2026 is the last Sunday of October, when Spain ends daylight saving time. At 01:00 UTC, clocks go back from 03:00 CEST (UTC+2) to 02:00 CET (UTC+1).
- The deadline of 02:30 UTC falls after that change, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
- 02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **Monday, 26 October 2026, at 07:59** Madrid time.

- **The date:** The last Sunday of October 2026 is **25 October**.
- **Pacific Time:** US daylight saving time doesn't end until 1 November 2026. So on 25 October, California is still on PDT (UTC−7). 23:59 PDT is 06:59 UTC on 26 October.
- **Madrid:** EU daylight saving time ends on 25 October 2026, earlier that same Sunday. By the deadline, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). 06:59 UTC is 07:59 CET.

The two regions change their clocks on different dates, so the usual 9-hour gap is temporarily 8 hours.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The US ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday in November, which in 2026 is **November 1**. The switch happens at 2:00 AM, so by noon Eastern Time is on standard time (EST, UTC−5).

Lima uses Peru Time (UTC−5) all year with no daylight saving. At that moment both are UTC−5, so noon Eastern equals noon in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **January 1, 2027, at 21:00** Tokyo time.

1. **AoE ("Anywhere on Earth")** is UTC−12.
2. **December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE** is the same moment as January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC−12.
3. **In UTC:** add 12 hours, giving January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.
4. **In Tokyo (JST, UTC+9, no daylight saving time):** add 9 hours, giving January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **2:00 AM on October 5, 2026, New York time**.

- **Sydney:** Australian daylight saving starts on the first Sunday of October, which is October 4, 2026. So on October 5, Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11). That makes 5:00 PM Sydney time equal to 06:00 UTC on October 5.
- **New York:** US daylight saving runs until November 1, 2026, so New York is on EDT (UTC−4). 06:00 UTC is therefore 02:00 on October 5.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
